question.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $A$ given below.
Which entries of $A$ could be replaced by $0$ in order to get a matrix in row echelon form?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that by replacing $a_{12}$, $a_{34}$, and $a_{44}$ with $0$, we get a matrix in row echelon form:

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\,\longrightarrow\,\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

The nonzero rows have leading entries in columns 3, 4, in strictly increasing order, and all zero rows are at the bottom. The other options will not give us a matrix in row echelon form.
